- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–4% to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use lagged 3-day average as anchor.
- Model consistently underestimates true price drops after a 3–5 day downtrend; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast during such periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period volatility; apply 1–2% upward adjustment if sentiment is positive in last 3 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.2–0.33 spikes, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 0.1–0.3 in next 3–5 days.
